subject.title: fix(browser): keep guarded CDP sockets on validated endpoints [AI]

question: Should guarded `existing-session` profiles with an explicit remote `cdpUrl` fail closed and require the regular `openclaw` driver, rather than attach through Chrome MCP without a pin-preserving transport?
rationale: The implementation is a deliberate security boundary choice, not a mechanical correction: retaining the old Chrome MCP subprocess handoff would allow a re-resolved destination after policy approval, while rejecting it changes existing strict-profile behavior.

options.title: Accept fail-closed guarded CDP
options.body: Approve the documented migration to the regular driver for guarded remote endpoints, keeping the approved DNS destination bound to the socket.

options.title: Design a pin-preserving MCP path
options.body: Pause merge and require a relay or transport that can carry the approved lookup across the Chrome MCP subprocess boundary.

options.title: Retain legacy attachment
options.body: Restore the Chrome MCP fallback only if maintainers explicitly accept the unpinned-security tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed guarded CDP
recommendation.body: Approve the documented migration to the regular driver for guarded remote endpoints, keeping the approved DNS destination bound to the socket.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to the PR and authored the concrete review requirements that led to the final fail-closed design.
